parole.significato: screw, bolt, a threaded metal fastener
parole.testo: A Turkic borrowing, likely borrowed from Ottoman Turkish بورغی (burɣu, “screw, auger”).

parole.significato: bundle, a cloth tied up for carrying things other than cloths
parole.testo: From Turkic languages, in consequence of the Mongol pressure and again after the Ottoman territory gains from Ottoman Turkish بوغچه (boğça, bohça).
From a Turkic language. Compare Karakhanid تُرْكْ (türk), Ottoman Turkish ترك (türk) etc.
Borrowed from Turkic, from Proto-Turkic *xātun. The earliest Arabic attestations of the word appear in Turkic contexts.

A pre-Mamluk Turkic borrowing. This word has later been borrowed again into the Egyptian dialect as قَزَق (qazaq, “pole”) from its version in Ottoman Turkish قازیق (kazık, “pale, stake, post driven into the ground”).

A pre-Mamluk Turkic borrowing, from a cognate of Ottoman Turkish طوپوز (topuz, “iron mace”). Assuming it is Arabic, singulative noun from عَرَب (ʕarab), عَرْب (ʕarb), the verbal nouns of عَرَبَ (ʕaraba, “to flow sharply”). The ultimate origin is subject to discussion, see Turkish araba for the possible Turkic origin.
